description: The whole of what the webview may ask the Rust shell to do: SIXTY-THREE entries, and nothing else. Two are core event permissions — `core:event:allow-listen` and `core:event:allow-unlisten`, which are exactly what `@tauri-apps/api/event`'s `listen()` and the unlisten function it returns invoke (`plugin:event|listen` / `plugin:event|unlisten`); the webview imports nothing else from Tauri but `invoke`, which needs no core grant for this app's own commands. `core:default` is deliberately NOT granted: it would hand the webview the live tray, menu and resources surfaces (`plugin:tray|new`, `plugin:menu|set_as_app_menu`, `plugin:resources|close`, …) and `plugin:event|emit`, which lets a webview forge a `state:changed` that Rust-side listeners receive. Sixty are this app's own commands: the EIGHTEEN engine operations (every engine invocation is constructed Rust-side in `src/engine.rs` from a typed operation enum — the webview has NO shell permission of any kind and `tauri-plugin-shell` is not a dependency), B6 adding `engine_schedule_verify`, which is MUTATING: it re-issues the engine-side kickstart, so the live launchd job runs the engine; and Phase E (E12) adding `engine_update_check` — `update --check --json`, the Settings screen's "Check now" — which is NOT mutating (its one write is the engine's own update-check record), takes no operand, and leaves the request to the engine (one anonymous GET of the project's latest GitHub release); the webview itself still reaches no remote host; and v0.3.0 (plan M8) adding the four calendar operations, none with an operand — `engine_calendar_status` and `engine_calendar_list` (reads: the calendar configuration and last scheduled reads; the Mac calendars and the configured links, never a link URL), `engine_calendar_test` (reads every configured source now; not mutating) and `engine_calendar_connect_mac` (MUTATING: installs and re-signs the Calendar Reader helper copy and raises the Calendar permission dialog; off macOS it refuses before any spawn), each with its own bound (30 s, 30 s, 75 s, 150 s). Provider fallback PR 3 adds five `provider` operations, every one MUTATING and bounded: `engine_provider_key_set` (the pasted key reaches the engine on STDIN only — never argv, an error or a log line; 19 s), `engine_provider_key_migrate` (an index; 19 s), `engine_provider_key_delete` (a key id, `k-` and 12 lowercase hex; 15 s), `engine_provider_key_scrub_backup` (holds the settings save lock across the call; 15 s) and `engine_provider_reset` (an index, or a label written to STDIN, never argv; 15 s). PR 3 final round 1 DROPPED two engine commands no app code called: `engine_config_validate` (it returned the engine's report verbatim, `normalized` with every literal `apiKey` included, for any absolute file the webview named, the real `config.json` among them) and `engine_provider_key_delete_all` (one call deleted every app key, around uninstall's kept-schedule refusal and consent); their operations stay Rust-side, for the settings guard, the candidate check and uninstall's key leg, and `tests/capability.rs` pins both refused. `provider test` has NO command of its own: it takes a candidate file path, and only the candidate-staging command reaches it — `provider_candidate_check` (P3-M1-T2), which takes the candidate as JSON TEXT and a closed mode (`"validate"`, or a Test's provider index and the bound its `config validate` row reports, capped at 30 minutes), never a path; it refuses before staging a calendar link address and any literal key other than the redaction placeholder at a key slot (`config_read` shows the placeholder in place of a stored key, so any other value was typed in; the save path refuses it anyway), stages the candidate itself (0600 in the app's 0700 candidate folder, under its own `provider-check-` name, removed on every outcome), runs `config validate --file` or `provider test --file --index` over it, and writes nothing to the real config (a Test is MUTATING and takes the in-flight guard; a validate does not). P3-M4-T3 adds Replace's Rust-owned pending-reset store, three commands each taking a label and the NEW key id (`k-` and 12 lowercase hex), never a path: `provider_pending_reset_add` records a `pre-save` reset in the app's own `pending-resets.json` and runs `provider reset` with the label on STDIN, `provider_pending_reset_flush` moves it to `post-save` after the save and resets again, and `provider_pending_reset_drop` discards an unsaved replacement, deleting its key (`provider key delete`) only when the saved config's `config validate` rows reference it nowhere. Then T11's three shell commands (`state_snapshot` reads the engine and derives the schedule state; `open_today` raises the window, for which the webview has no window permission at all; `app_quit` exits, and refuses until the Quit notice has been shown this session); B5's five: `read_latest_briefing` / `read_archived_briefing` READ the two engine files a briefing lives in (the archive command takes a validated calendar date, never a path; both join onto the paths `status --json` reports and never write), and `config_read` / `config_save` / `config_offer_notify_auto` are the app's ONE config-write path (JSON text in, never a path; `status --json`'s `paths.configPath`, never Tauri's config dir; engine-validated, atomic, `.bak` kept; `transcripts` and a literal API key cannot be changed); B6's four (T17): `access_snapshot` reports which macOS-protected folders this config reaches and what `doctor --json` says about them, `access_probe` READS ONE of four fixed protected folders from this process (a closed enum, never a path — it is the macOS prompt trigger and the revocation detector), `access_reveal_engine` reveals the managed engine copy whose path it re-reads from `schedule status --json`, and `access_open_settings` opens ONE of three fixed System Settings URLs chosen by a closed enum; and B7's two (T18): `notify_status` reads the app's notification opt-in record, the ENGINE's resolved `notify` value and the suppression log, and `notify_set_enabled` records the explained ask's answer — neither can post a notification. B8 adds four (T16 + dev 63): `config_create` is the FIRST-config path — the wizard's one write, JSON text in and never a path, engine-validated through `config validate --file`, EXCLUSIVELY created (anything already at the name — a file, a symlink, a racing `daily-briefing init` — is refused as `alreadyExists`, never replaced), with a literal `provider.api.apiKey` and any `transcripts` block refused outright; and the three `cli_shim_*` commands (the Settings screen's explicit "install command-line tool" action): `cli_shim_status` reads what sits at `/usr/local/bin/daily-briefing`, `cli_shim_install` writes a symlink there to the managed engine copy (target re-read from `schedule status --json`, never webview-supplied; a foreign file at the name is refused), and `cli_shim_remove` deletes only a symlink whose target is the managed copy or another name in the engine's state directory — none of the three takes an operand, and a permission refusal returns the exact manual command instead of escalating. B25 adds two (T25): `uninstall_preview` reads what an uninstall would remove (the app's own records, the window-state file, and — from `status --json` and `schedule status --json`, never the webview — the engine state dir's bounded list and the background scheduler's facts), and `uninstall_execute` performs it: FIRST the background scheduler, which it never unregisters itself (no `launchctl`, no `systemctl`) but hands to the engine's own `schedule uninstall --invoker app`, with `--take-over` only when its closed `schedule` operand says `removeAny` (`keep` calls nothing, and the default `removeOwn` refuses, without calling the engine, a scheduler this app did not install); then the app's OWN autostart entry via T19's plugin `disable()`, the app's OWN files, ONLY behind its first explicit boolean consent operand the engine-state entries, which mirror `scripts/uninstall.sh`'s `$SUPPORT`-rooted list token for token (set-equality with a test-time parse of the script, `tests/uninstall.rs`), plus on Linux the managed engine copy after its ownership checks, and ONLY behind its second the settings the engine's `configPath` folder holds (a key file a readable config names when it sits directly in that folder, `config.json`, `config.json.bak`, then the folder only if empty) — never a recursive delete of the support directory, and never a path from the webview. Phase E M5b adds two (T19 reworked): `autostart_set_enabled` turns the login item ON or OFF — the Settings toggle AND the setup wizard's last step — taking one boolean and nothing else (ON is the plugin's `enable()` followed, on macOS, by adding `AssociatedBundleIdentifiers` = the bundle id to the plist it wrote; OFF is its `disable()`), and `autostart_wizard_default` READS the app's login-item record and the real state for the wizard's pre-tick; neither takes a path, and nothing at launch calls either. v0.3.0 (plan M8) adds three for a calendar LINK's Rust side: `calendar_link_write` takes a link id (grammar `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$`, `macos` reserved) and its URL (https or webcal, no whitespace or control character, at most 4096 bytes — never echoed, logged or returned) and writes ONLY `<state>/calendar/links/<id>.url`, 0600 in a 0700 folder, atomically, refusing a symlinked, foreign-owned or loose folder and a non-regular file at the name, at most ten link files, under the state dir `status --json` reports; `calendar_link_remove` takes the id alone and removes that link file and the link's entry in `calendar.links`; and `calendar_config_save` takes the `calendar` block as JSON text and replaces that one key through the same config-write path as `config_save` (engine-validated, atomic, `.bak` kept, every other field preserved), refusing before any spawn a key spelled `url`, a URL in a link's name or owner or an email entry, a bad or duplicate link id and more than ten links. None takes a path. The briefing redesign (A-M1) adds the app-preference store's two: `app_prefs_get` reads and `app_prefs_set` changes the first name (used only in the greeting; trimmed, at most 40 characters, no control or bidi-control character, validated Rust-side) and the "show the briefing as slides" switch in the app's own `app-prefs.json` (0600, under the app's data folder) — neither takes a path, spawns anything or sends the name to the engine. The briefing redesign's B1 adds one live git read, `repos_status`: a READ (no in-flight guard; one check in flight is its own latch), gated in Rust by the main window's visibility, the deck's current slide and a stat of each repo's git metadata, so a quiet minute spawns nothing, with four exceptions: on the launchpad the "Not committed" status runs every minute, with nothing held for the page, after a failed check, a full check runs every minute until one succeeds, a repo the last check answered `unknown` is retried (after 1, 2, 4, then 5 minutes while it keeps timing out, and every 5 minutes otherwise), and a repo with more than 2 000 entries under `refs/` counts as changed every minute; it takes the page's cards (each key and its hex tokens), the named branches, the page date, the reason for the ask and the current slide, validated Rust-side (at most 64 cards and 64 branch entries, keys of at most 80 characters, tokens of 1 to 40 hex digits, at most 512 per card and 4096 in all, branch names of at most 255 bytes, no control or format character) and written to the engine's `repos status --json` on STDIN, never argv; bounded at 30 s; its reply crosses without the engine-only list of repo paths and without any member the reply types do not declare, and nothing the engine writes to stderr reaches the webview. It takes no path and writes nothing. The briefing redesign's wave 2 (C) adds the live calendar details' four, none taking a path or a URL: `calendar_details_open` asks for one live read of today's calendar details, gated in Rust (the window shown, the calendar slide or the launchpad current, the ask's reason, one read in flight), which runs `calendar details --json` through a sealed path whose output never becomes an engine outcome, and answers the held or new list with NO URL in it (only each event's Join host) — the remembered command-link URLs stay in Rust memory and go back to the engine on STDIN only; `calendar_details_get` returns one event's people and notes from Rust's in-memory map by handle and reads nothing; `calendar_join` opens one event's meeting link by handle, after Rust re-validates it (https, no userinfo, no written port; a host outside the known meeting services needs the webview's confirmation), through the opener's free function — the webview never names a URL and the opener's error is never forwarded; and `calendar_app_open` launches the Calendar app by bundle id on today (`/usr/bin/open -b com.apple.iCal ical://date/<now, UTC>?method=show`, built from Rust's clock alone), macOS only, taking nothing from any event. The briefing redesign's B2 adds the opening commands' five, none taking a URL, a path or a command, and each answering a fixed code rather than a process's or a sink's words: `open_github` opens one held GitHub target by handle, with the GitHub links switch on and after Rust re-judges the target (https, github.com, no userinfo, query or fragment) through the opener's free function, `copy_push_command` copies the push command of held branches by handle, its text built in Rust and never returned, through the clipboard plugin's Rust API (that plugin is registered so the write has its state, and its six live commands, `write_text`, `read_text`, `read_image`, `write_image`, `write_html` and `clear`, are refused to the webview and pinned one by one in `tests/capability.rs`), and, macOS only, `editor_list` reads the installed editors and the project inventory (project keys and labels, never a folder), `editor_open` launches a closed-enum editor on one held folder by handle (`/usr/bin/open -b <bundle id> <folder>`, no shell) after Rust re-checks the folder, and `editor_choice_set` remembers a project's editor in the app's own `app-prefs.json` by its stable key. The briefing redesign's A2 adds one read, `read_latest_summary`: it takes two 64-hex identities (`pageHash`, `pageVersion`), never a path, and is no new engine operation (`status --json` is its only spawn); it re-checks the latest page's identity, reads only the constructed versioned sidecar under `paths.briefingsDir` with a capped, no-symlink read, revalidates every stored point and sentence in Rust (stored keys by syntax only, so card membership is the webview's), and answers the record or ordinary absence with fixed warning codes; no raw response, provider config or filesystem error crosses, and an engine client that failed at startup is absence too. It writes nothing. The LAST ONE is `tauri-plugin-autostart`'s `autostart:allow-is-enabled` (T19): the Settings toggle must reflect REAL state via `is_enabled()`, a stat of the plist, operand-free. The plugin's own `allow-enable` / `allow-disable` are NO LONGER granted (M5b): its `enable()` writes an unbranded plist, so every ON goes through `autostart_set_enabled` instead. NOTHING is granted for `tauri-plugin-notification` although it IS registered (the Rust-side post needs its managed state): its three live commands (`notify`, `request_permission`, `is_permission_granted`) are refused to the webview — posting is a Rust decision driven by the watcher, and `tests/capability.rs` pins the refusals as it does the tray's. NOTHING is granted for `tauri-plugin-window-state`: its persistence is entirely Rust-side. NOTHING is granted for `tauri-plugin-opener` either, and it is never registered on the builder, so its commands do not exist at runtime — `src/access.rs` calls its FREE functions Rust-side. The caller-supplied operands (`run --json-out <name>`, and since PR 3 a provider `--index`, a key `--id` and a reset label) are validated in Rust before any spawn. This is deny-by-default only because `build.rs` declares an app ACL manifest — see the note there. capabilities/README.md carries the rationale, the B1 first-match-ceiling history this replaces, and the Known gaps.
